title: Short Stuff: William King
summary: Short Stuff episode on William Rufus DeVane King, early Democratic congressman, diplomat, and Alabama senator who served as Franklin Pierce's vice president and was sworn in on Cuban soil in 1853 because of tuberculosis. The hosts cover his career and plantation in Alabama (including his role in naming Selma), and his reported relationship with President James Buchanan, which they say historians now widely view as evidence Buchanan was gay, citing Jim Loehr's book and an Andrew Jackson nickname. They close by noting King died weeks after returning to US soil and that the US went four years without a vice president, and criticize Franklin Pierce's presidency.
topics: Andrew Jackson nicknames Miss Nancy Aunt Fancy

segments.title: Introduction and William King's early career
segments.summary: The hosts introduce William Rufus DeVane King, describing his career as a congressman, diplomat, and long-serving Alabama senator, and his reputation as a middle-of-the-road, conciliatory Democrat.

segments.title: Plantation, Selma, and Senate career
segments.summary: King moved to Alabama, became a plantation owner who held many enslaved people, named his plantation Chestnut Hill, and was involved in naming the city of Selma, Alabama. He became Alabama senator for twenty-nine years.

segments.title: King and James Buchanan's relationship and historical attitudes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss historians' views that President James Buchanan was gay and that his relationship with King was an open secret in Washington, including Andrew Jackson's nicknames for them and a surviving letter. They discuss how this reflects that attitudes were not simply progressing over time.
topics: Andrew Jackson nicknames Miss Nancy Aunt Fancy

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Pre-break transition promising the Cuba oath story after a quick break.

segments.title: Oath of office sworn in Cuba
segments.summary: King became vice president under Franklin Pierce in 1852 but fell ill with tuberculosis and went to Havana. Congress passed an Act allowing him to take the oath in Cuba, and he was sworn in March 1853 at Matanzas, becoming the only US elected official sworn in off US soil.

segments.title: Death and Franklin Pierce
segments.summary: King returned to Alabama and died in April 1853, the day after reaching US soil. The hosts note the vice presidency went unfilled for four years and criticize Franklin Pierce's presidency.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and point to the show website and social media.
